clue.text: Party member left in the same place, one dumped

indicators.note: dumped means thrown out, so the letter for one is dropped from the Latin word

parts.note: ibidem is Latin for 'in the same place', used in footnotes
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A party member stays put on the left while one colleague gets ditched.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a centrist British party; 'one dumped' tells you which letter of the Latin footnote term goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lib Dem belongs to the Liberal Democrats, a British political party.

clue.text: American lyricist said to be someone still developing technique?

indicators.note: said to be signals that the lyricist's surname is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Alan Jay Lerner wrote the lyrics for My Fair Lady

explanation.surface: A famous American songwriter is described as still a novice at his craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil or novice is someone still acquiring a skill, such as a driver with L-plates.

clue.text: Hot dish served up in Italian party

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: LAB is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A spicy meal is dished out at an Italian celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Interpret old poet

parts.note: EX means former or old
Ezra Pound was an American modernist poet

explanation.surface: A writer from an earlier era is asked to explain things.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to explain or set out the meaning of something in detail.

clue.text: Appeal to protect tree by hospital power supply years ago

indicators.note: to protect means to surround and shield, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: a call is an appeal or request

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground

explanation.surface: A campaign to save a tree beside a hospital, set against an old electricity scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: CALDER HALL in Cumbria was the world's first commercial-scale nuclear power station, opened in 1956 and now closed.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cumbrian nuclear station once generated electricity for the national grid, but was shut in 2003.

clue.text: A writer enthralling mum, being transformative?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
MA is a word for mother

explanation.surface: A writer captivates their mother and seems to be changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a noun here, a creature, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-man is a creature midway in evolution from primate to human, so a being in transition.

clue.text: Profane girl lacking seriousness

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
shallow means superficial, lacking depth or seriousness

explanation.surface: A girl is called irreverent and frivolous.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic verb means to desecrate or treat something holy without reverence.

clue.text: Female in something underground before work that is well above ground level

definitions.text: that is well above ground level

indicators.note: before means coming earlier, so this piece precedes the next
in means placed inside, so one letter goes within the other word

parts.note: a root grows underground
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A woman goes down a tunnel before a job high up.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a building's covering is high above the street.

clue.text: I start life that's formed with tiny particle?

definitions.text: I start life that's formed with tiny particle?

indicators.note: formed means shaped or made up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ion is a charged atomic particle

explanation.surface: A new being announces that it began when something very small combined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges I START LIFE plus ION; the whole clue also describes the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Conception begins when sperm meets egg, a tiny cell, starting a new life.

clue.text: See 4
In advance, give a sort of force to claim

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before or in advance
tension is a pulling force in physics

explanation.surface: Ahead of time, someone applies pressure to stake a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretension is a claim or aspiration to something, such as a title or status.

clue.text: Substitute powdering her nose, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: powdering her nose is a euphemism for visiting the lavatory, so she is in the loo

explanation.surface: A stand-in is apparently off in the ladies' room.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-derived phrase means instead of, taking the place of something else.

clue.text: Right-wing bunch that was organised by one proverbially mad?

definitions.meaning: the American conservative populist movement named after the Boston protest

definitions.text: that was organised by one proverbially mad?
definitions.meaning: the Mad Hatter hosts the famous gathering in Alice in Wonderland, and 'mad as a hatter' is proverbial

explanation.surface: A conservative faction is said to be run by a lunatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the US political movement and the Wonderland gathering carry this name.

clue.text: Cold part in which fish is taken by one reptile

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in which means the following pieces go inside the part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: taken by means joined to, so the two pieces sit together

parts.note: cod is a fish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A chilly scene where someone takes a fish to feed a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: This large, long-jawed creature is a reptile of tropical rivers.

clue.text: Stardust is evident in court — one believes everything has been planned

definitions.text: one believes everything has been planned

indicators.note: evident in means seen within, so these pieces sit inside the court

parts.note: Alvin Stardust was a British glam-rock singer of the 1970s

explanation.surface: A celebrity appears in court, where a believer in fate waits.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of this Reformed tradition hold to predestination, that God has ordained every outcome.

clue.text: Small piece of paper in sink

definitions.meaning: a small strip of paper, such as a betting or payment chit
to fall or decline, as standards or prices do

explanation.surface: A scrap of paper lies in the basin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a paper chit and to decline or fall lower.

clue.text: Education's No 1 place to the West?

definitions.text: Education's No 1 place to the West?

indicators.note: in an across clue, to the West means read leftward, backwards
No 1 means number one, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to lay is to place or put down

explanation.surface: A boast that a certain university is the top educational venue in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' takes E; with LAY that makes ELAY, which 'to the West' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ivy League university in Connecticut is a leading Western seat of learning.

clue.text: Long day in which one has little energy when books are balanced?

indicators.note: in which one has means the pair contains the next piece

parts.note: to long is to yearn
E is the abbreviation for energy, little because it is short

explanation.surface: A tiring, drawn-out day when the accounts are finally squared.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are closed and reconciled at the close of the financial calendar.

clue.text: Colon now having a turn with obstruction

parts.note: a spin is a turn
a wall is an obstruction

explanation.surface: Someone's bowel trouble now involves a twist and a blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colon' is not the gut: it is Colón, the Panamanian port, whose earlier name was this.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panamanian city now called Colón was founded under this American name.

clue.text: Routine changes where life develops

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daily routine shifts as new life grows.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means within the womb, where an embryo grows.

clue.text: Sediment outside back of the church drains

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: lees are the sediment in wine

indicators.note: back of means the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Deposits gather round the rear of a church's drainage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drains' is a noun: things that drain, here bloodsuckers.
explanation.definitionFit: These bloodsucking worms draw blood from their hosts, figuratively parasites that exhaust resources.

clue.text: Mug takes stupid risks injecting drug

indicators.note: injecting means putting into, so the drug goes inside
stupid means senseless or muddled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A fool takes daft chances by shooting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges RISKS to KISSR, into which 'injecting' puts E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang words for the face, the mouth in particular.

clue.text: Condition is put into agreement for one seeking to avoid conflict

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so these pieces go within

parts.note: a pact is an agreement
IF introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A clause is added to a treaty by someone wanting peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rejects war or violence tries to keep clear of conflict.

clue.text: Nude is forced to get minimal attire

indicators.note: forced means pushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naked person is compelled to put on the barest clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is the least one can wear, clothing kept to a minimum.

clue.text: Françoise who played tennis, ace on grass

parts.note: Françoise Durr was a French tennis player who won the 1967 French Open
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A French tennis star scores an ace on a grass court.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of sorghum, a cereal grass grown for grain in warm countries.

clue.text: Group meeting this month, one absolutely fixed

parts.note: a set is a group
inst. is short for instant, an old commercial term for this month

explanation.surface: A group's meeting this month has one item firmly decided.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carved into rock is permanent and cannot be changed.

clue.text: Imprisoned in Exeter, a human demon

indicators.note: imprisoned in means held within, so the letters lie inside the words

explanation.surface: A monstrous person is locked up in Exeter, a cathedral city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu myth this serpent-headed figure swallows the sun or moon to cause eclipses.

clue.text: Lovers being brusque almost after social function

indicators.note: after means following, so this piece comes behind

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: terse means curt or brusque

explanation.surface: Romantic partners turn short-tempered after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: People who dote are fond admirers, infatuated with someone.

clue.text: Confused situation created by men in service

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A muddle is caused by soldiers in a religious service.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or swamp, figuratively a complicated mess hard to escape.
